name: HD 80606
title: HD 80606 b: the Rossiter–McLaughlin effect
notes: Real data: the velocity compilation of EXOTIC’s sample data holds two partial transits, SOPHIE on 2009 February 14 and HIRES on 2009 June 5, each its own dataset with a jitter. v sin i★ and the projected obliquity λ are free with the orbit (velocities and five mid-times). Rp/R★ is held at 0.1001 (Winn et al. 2009): the TESS radius is diluted by HD 80607. The anomaly uses limb darkening of the 390–690 nm band. Hébrard et al. (2010) found λ = 42 ± 8° from a full transit that is not in this file.

warnings: The posterior of jitter (rv6) runs into the lower edge of its prior. That is fine if the edge is physical (i = 90°, zero jitter or mass: read the result as a limit); otherwise widen the prior.
The posterior of jitter (rv7) runs into the lower edge of its prior. That is fine if the edge is physical (i = 90°, zero jitter or mass: read the result as a limit); otherwise widen the prior.
e and ω are -0.98 correlated: fit √e cos ω and √e sin ω instead, or fix one.
